- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce subsequent forecast values by 5–10% to account for volatility decay.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, avoid over-optimistic tail ends — cap final 5–7 days at 1–2% below recent 10-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.3 → +0.6), reduce forecast volatility in subsequent periods by 10–20%.
